units.label: Listening Test 6 · Part B

questions.prompt:
You hear a training for optometrists.
 What does the instructor clarify about the training ?
A. That it is for optometrists seeking a specialty in the field
B. That it is for optometrists wanting a review of primary eye care
C. That it is for optometrists currently still completing their training

You hear a nurse explaining a new protocol for patient handover. .
 The new protocol for patient handover prioritises
A. communication between the nurses on the case
B. communication between nurses and patients
C. communication between the nurses and the doctors

You hear a nurse talking to a patient about his upcoming hospital stay. .
 What does she describe to the patient?
A. A written document about eight main areas of care after surgery
B. A written document about how families can help the patient during
 recovery
C. A written document about what patients can do to be safe

You hear a surgeon talking about an optional training. .
 What does the surgeon explain about the medical problem?
A. Its prognosis is more complicated than that of similar cancers
B. Its prognosis is comparable to that of similar cancers
C. Its prognosis is not as promising as that of similar cancers

You hear a doctor explaining the side effects of a treatment to a patient. .

 What does the doctor suggest the patient do?
A. Purchase a thermometer to keep track of his temperature
B. Take the prescribed treatment every four weeks
C. Avoid any infections as much as possible during treatment

You hear an intern ask a senior doctor about a patient’s treatment. .
 The senior doctor explains to the intern
A. A series of reasons why this particular treatment is being used
B. A series of ways in which the patient is not responding well
C. A series of ways that a patient could respond to the treatment

units.label: Listening Test 6 · Part C

questions.prompt:
What does the speaker say has changed in terms of allergies and
 children?
A. More children are presenting with food allergies.
B. More children are presenting with allergies in general.
C. More children are presenting with an allergy to peanuts.

According to the speaker, children with this allergy initially
A. Present with a less severe reaction
B. Present with a more severe reaction
C. Present with other allergies or conditions

What is the objective of the first treatment approach being researched?
A. To have children build up tolerance by starting to eat a wider
 variety of foods
B. To have children build up tolerance by starting to eat small
 amounts of the allergen
C. To have children build up tolerance by starting to eat large
 amounts of the allergen

How will researchers know how children have reacted to the treatment?
A. Through observing them for a few hours at the hospital
B. Through recording them for a few hours at a time
C. Through phone calls and having them visit the clinic

According to the speaker, why is the current treatment for this condition
 difficult for patients?
A. Because it requires persistent watchfulness
B. Because many people like to eat foods with the allergen
C. Because many people are unaware of the condition

What is one reason for the treatment method used in the second study?
A. Because many patients do not have the time to add the allergen
 to their diet
B. Because many patients have a strong reaction to the taste or
 smell of the allergen
C. Because many patients prefer not to make any changes to their
 current diets

According to the interviewee, what problem was the research trying to
 address?
A. The damage done to the transplanted organ during surgery
B. The amount of time required to complete the transplant
C. The loss of blood supply to the transplanted organ during surgery

What factor did the researcher take into account when choosing which
 tool to use?
A. The cost of overall procedure
B. The cost of the tool itself
C. The ease of access to the tool

How did the placebo procedure differ from the experimental one?
A. The blood pressure cuff was tightened more
B. The blood pressure cuff was not tightened
C. The blood pressure cuff was not used

According to the researcher, why was the research done over a number of
 years?
A. Because the effectiveness of the kidney declines gradually
B. Because there were many patients involved in the study
C. Because it took a long time to analyze all of the information

The interviewer says that the procedure has the potential to…
A. Extend the lifespan of all patients by years
B. Increase the cost to the NHS by quite a lot
C. Make the lives of transplant patients better

The research would like to figure out why the procedure...
A. Has not always received positive results
B. Has not been thoroughly researched
C. Has not received a lot of attention by doctors
